data.title: Piano Keys
data.author: gametorch
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了钢琴白键和黑键宽度排列的问题。由于黑键宽度相同且白键前端宽度一致，后端宽度无法完全相同。文章提出了几种优化方案，以最小化白键后端宽度的最大差异。初始方案如设置不同宽度组合，达到最大差异为B/2、B/6、B/8等。最佳传统方案是"B/12方案"，最大差异仅为B/12。进一步放宽条件，允许黑键和白键前端宽度变化，提出一种单位划分法，将一个八度分为878472单位，优化后最大差异显著减小，白键为0.0181英寸，黑键为0.0127英寸。这种优化方案在实际制造中更精确，显著减少宽度差异。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：钢琴键盘设计，特别是黑键和白键的布局及其合理性。

不同观点：
• **prmph** 认为当前的钢琴键盘设计没有问题，并提出假设：如果把黑键放在白键后面并占据白键的一部分宽度，并不影响弹奏。他质疑为什么白键后部的宽度需要一致，并指出 pianists 不会按到白键的后部。

• **bruce343434** 回应称，在他的钢琴上，黑键的宽度和白键后部的宽度是一样的，这是通过调整黑键的位置实现的，而不是将黑键完全置于白键中间。

• **kazinator** 认为钢琴设计中并没有对白键后部宽度过于精细的要求，实际设计中更关注黑键的宽度和分布。他解释了黑键和白键布局的历史设计方法，并指出这种设计并不是完全对称的，例如 E-F 之间的分割并不完全在两个黑键中间。

• **ralfd** 表示对原文内容不理解，建议需要更多图片来帮助理解。

• **moefh** 认为黑键的传统布局是将八度音分为两个部分（C-D-E 和 F-G-A-B），然后根据这些部分均匀放置黑键，并指出白键在这些部分内有“镜像”关系，例如 C 和 E 的位置关系。他认为实际的钢琴键盘符合这种描述。

• **NooneAtAll3** 希望文章中能有标注音符的图片，并希望看到按键宽度的示意图，以便更好地理解讨论内容。

• **ajuc** 认为钢琴键盘设计不规则，给演奏者带来了记忆不同和弦位置的负担，例如 C 大调和 D 大调的和弦形状不同。他建议可以采用更规则的设计，例如将一个八度分为 6 个白键和 6 个黑键。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一在于钢琴键盘布局的历史设计合理性，特别是黑键和白键的宽度与分布是否应该一致，以及这种不规则布局是否给学习者带来了不必要的困难。
• 一些评论者（如 prmph 和 kazinator）认为当前设计没有问题，而另一些人（如 ajuc）则认为可以采用更规则的设计来简化学习和演奏。
• 图片和视觉示例在讨论中被多次提及，显示出视觉辅助在理解键盘布局复杂性方面的重要性。

44576183.article_content:
Piano Keys
If you've ever looked closely at a piano keyboard you may have
noticed that the widths of the white keys are not all the same
at the back ends (where they pass between the black keys).  Of
course, if you think about it for a minute, it's clear they
couldn't possibly all be the same width, assuming the black keys
are all identical (with non-zero width) and the white keys all
have equal widths at the front ends, because the only simultaneous
solution of 3W=3w+2b and 4W=4w+3b is with b=0.
After realizing this I started noticing different pianos and how
they accommodate this little problem in linear programming.  Let W
denote the widths of the white keys at the front, and let B denote
the widths of the black keys.  Then let a, b,..., g (assigned to
their musical equivalents) denote the widths of the white keys
at the back.  Assuming a perfect fit, it's impossible to have
a = b = ... = g.  The best we can do is try to minimize the
greatest difference between any two of these keys.
One crude approach would be to set d=g=a=(W-B) and b=c=e=f=(W-B/2),
which gives a maximum difference of B/2 between the widths of any
two white keys (at the back ends).  This isn't a very good solution,
and I've never seen an actual keyboard based on this pattern
(although some cartoon pianos seem to have this pattern).  A better
solution is to set a=b=c=e=f=g=(W-3B/4) and d=(W-B/2).  With this
arrangement, all but one of the white keys have the same width at
the back end, and the discrepancy of the "odd" key (the key of "d")
is only B/4.  Some actual keyboards (e.g., the Roland HP-70) use
this pattern.
Another solution is to set c=d=e=f=b=(W-2B/3) and g=a=(W-5B/6),
which results in a maximum discrepancy of just B/6.  There are
several other combinations that give this same maximum discrepancy,
and actual keyboards based on this pattern are not uncommon.
If we set c=e=(W-5B/8) and a=b=d=f=g=(W-3B/4) we have a maximum
discrepancy of only B/8, and quite a few actual pianos use this
pattern as well.  However, the absolute optimum arrangement is to
set c=d=e=(W-2B/3) and f=g=a=b=(W-3B/4), which gives a maximum
discrepancy of just B/12.  This pattern is used on many keyboards,
e.g. the Roland PC-100.
The "B/12 solution" is the best possible given that all the black keys
are identical and all the white keys have equal widths at the front
ends.  For practical manufacturing purposes this is probably the
best approach.  However, suppose we relax those conditions and allow
variations in the widths of the black keys and in the widths of the
white keys at the front ends.  All we require is that the black
keys (in total) are allocated 5/12 of the octave.  On this basis,
what is the optimum arrangement, minimizing the maximum discrepancy
between any two widths of the same type?
Let A, B,...G denote the front-end widths of the white keys, and
let a#, c#, d#, f#, g# denote the widths of the black keys.  I
believe the optimum arrangement is given by dividing the octave
into 878472 units, and then setting
f=g=a=b=72156 units      c=d=e=74606 units      discrepancy=2450
f#=g#=a#=72520 units     c#=d#=74235 units      discrepancy=1715
F=G=A=B=126546 units     C=D=E=124096 units     discrepancy=2450
The maximum discrepancy between any two widths of the same class is
1/29.88 of the width of the average black key, which is less than
half the discrepancy for the "B/12 solution".
The max discrepancy is 1/358.56 of the total octave for the white
keys, and 1/512.22 for the black keys.  Since an octave is normally
about 6.5 inches, the max discrepancy is about 0.0181 inches for the
white keys and 0.0127 inches for the black keys.  (One peculiar fact
about this optimum arrangement is that the median point of the octave,
the boundary between f and f#, is exactly 444444 units up from the
start of the octave.)

data.title: Show HN: Am-I-vibing, detect agentic coding environments
data.author: ascorbic
data.article_summary: "am-i-vibing" 是一个用于检测代理编码环境和 AI 辅助工具的库。它帮助 CLI 工具和 Node 应用判断是否由 AI 代理执行，并做出相应调整，如改变输出格式或日志。该库支持多种 AI 工具，如 Claude Code、GitHub Copilot、Replit 等，并能识别三种环境类型：代理环境、交互环境和混合环境。通过提供的 API，开发者可以轻松检测当前环境类型并作出相应处理。此外，该库还提供了 CLI 工具，用于快速环境检测和调试。主要功能包括输出格式选择、特定环境类型检查、安静模式和调试模式等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用代理（agent）生成和运行代码的实践及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• barbazoo：认为代理生成的代码在运行时中体现其存在是不合适的。代理只是工具，开发者应亲自编写代码，特别是错误处理和消息提示，因为当凌晨3点收到警报时，代理无法帮忙。同时，人类易于理解的内容通常也易于LLM理解。

• Timwi：指出该方法存在多个缺点，包括不可靠性（项目文档中提到存在误报）、用户混淆（AI代理报告的内容与手动运行CLI工具的结果不一致）、以及用户无法手动访问功能。建议明确提供选项以启用新行为，并教导AI在适当情况下使用这些功能，而非依赖代理。

• 0xDEAFBEAD：认为当前的做法增加了供应链攻击的脆弱性，达到了不应有的程度。

• mrKola 和 fahrradflucht：对项目命名提出批评和替代建议，mrKola 戏谑地建议命名为 "vibrator"，fahrradflucht 则提出 "prompt-injection-toolkit" 作为替代。

• CaptainFever：认为该库设想的是合作性的结果，比如代码在检测到处于代理环境时提供额外上下文，但担心有人会利用此功能限制他人。在这种情况下，AI代理可能需要一个项目特定的“隐形模式”来保护用户。

• ritzaco：强烈反对该做法，认为代理应适应人类设计的工具或使用专门为代理设计的工具。让工具在人类和代理操作下表现不同只会导致混乱。

• ofirg：批评软件包命名不当，认为不应在项目获得实际使用后因压力而更改名称。

• petesergeant：对技术实现表现出兴趣，提到可能会通过monkey patch的方式让vitest在代理使用时显示完整差异。

• SudoSuccubus：对检测代理行为的尝试表示强烈反感，认为这种做法类似于学术界的“反作弊”系统，是徒劳的。强调应与未来技术合作，而不是抗拒。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于代理生成代码在运行时的影响、用户混淆以及潜在的安全风险。
• 部分评论集中在项目命名和命名恰当性的问题上。
• 部分评论表现出对技术改进的兴趣和建议，如明确启用新行为的选项和通过monkey patch增强工具功能。
• SudoSuccubus 的评论带有强烈的情绪，反对对代理行为的检测和限制尝试。

am-i-vibing
Detect agentic coding environments and AI assistant tools. This library allows CLI tools and Node apps to detect when they're being executed by AI agents. This enables them to adapt by, for example, providing different output formats or logs.
Installation
Install as library:
npm install am-i-vibing
Run as CLI tool:
npx am-i-vibing
import
{
detectAgenticEnvironment
}
from
"am-i-vibing"
;
const
result
=
detectAgenticEnvironment
(
)
;
console
.
log
(
`Detected:
${
result
.
name
}
(
${
result
.
type
}
)`
)
;

Aider
Bolt
Claude Code
Cursor
Gemini CLI
GitHub Copilot Agent

Environment Types
The library detects three main types of environments:
Agent
: Command was directly run by an AI agent (e.g. Claude Code, Codex CLI, Jules)
Interactive
: Interactive commands run inside an AI environment (e.g. Cursor terminal, Replit shell)
Hybrid
: Environments that combine both agentic and interactive features in the same session (e.g. Warp)
There may be false positives, such as if a user directly runs a command in an terminal opened by an AI tool, such as a Copilot terminal in VS Code.

CLI Options
-f, --format <json|text>
- Output format (default: text)
-c, --check <agent|interactive|hybrid>
- Check for specific environment type
-q, --quiet
- Only output result, no labels
-d, --debug
- Debug output with environment and process info
-h, --help
- Show help message
Exit Codes
0
- Agentic environment detected (or specific check passed)
1
- No agentic environment detected (or specific check failed)

• mrKola 和 fahrradflucht：对项目命名提出批评和替代建议，mrKola 戏谑地建议命名为 "vibrator"，fahrradflucht 则提出 "prompt-injection-toolkit" 作为替代。

• CaptainFever：认为该库设想的是合作性的结果，比如代码在检测到处于代理环境时提供额外上下文，但担心有人会利用此功能限制他人。在这种情况下，AI代理可能需要一个项目特定的“隐形模式”来保护用户。

• ritzaco：强烈反对该做法，认为代理应适应人类设计的工具或使用专门为代理设计的工具。让工具在人类和代理操作下表现不同只会导致混乱。

• ofirg：批评软件包命名不当，认为不应在项目获得实际使用后因压力而更改名称。

• petesergeant：对技术实现表现出兴趣，提到可能会通过monkey patch的方式让vitest在代理使用时显示完整差异。

• SudoSuccubus：对检测代理行为的尝试表示强烈反感，认为这种做法类似于学术界的“反作弊”系统，是徒劳的。强调应与未来技术合作，而不是抗拒。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于代理生成代码在运行时的影响、用户混淆以及潜在的安全风险。
• 部分评论集中在项目命名和命名恰当性的问题上。
• 部分评论表现出对技术改进的兴趣和建议，如明确启用新行为的选项和通过monkey patch增强工具功能。
• SudoSuccubus 的评论带有强烈的情绪，反对对代理行为的检测和限制尝试。

data.title: Hungary's oldest library is fighting to save books from a beetle infestation
data.author: smollett
data.article_summary: 匈牙利最古老的潘诺恩哈尔马修道院图书馆正努力拯救约10万本手抄书，这些书受到甲虫侵扰。药店甲虫（也称面包甲虫）不仅出现在食物中，还被书籍的胶水和淀粉吸引。为消灭甲虫，修复人员将书籍放入密封塑料袋，抽空氧气，注入氮气，经过六周处理希望彻底消灭甲虫。处理后，每本书将逐一检查和吸尘，受损书籍将进行后续修复。虽然最古老和珍稀的书未受影响，但任何损坏都被视为对文化和历史遗产的打击。

44583316.article_content:
Hungarian library is fighting to save books from beetles
Restoration workers are removing about 100,000 handbound books from their shelves and carefully placing them in crates, the start of a disinfection process that aims to kill the tiny beetles.
Europe
Hungary's oldest library is fighting to save 100,000 books from a beetle infestation
July 14, 2025
1:24 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
Books are kept in hermetically sealed plastic sacks for disinfection, at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary on July 3.
Bela Szandelszky/AP
hide caption
toggle caption
Bela Szandelszky/AP
PANNONHALMA, Hungary — Tens of thousands of centuries-old books are being pulled from the shelves of a medieval abbey in Hungary in an effort to save them from a beetle infestation that could wipe out centuries of history.
Books We Love
NPR staffers pick their favorite fiction reads of 2025 so far
The 1,000-year-old Pannonhalma Archabbey is a sprawling Benedictine monastery that is one of Hungary's oldest centers of learning and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Restoration workers are removing about 100,000 handbound books from their shelves and carefully placing them in crates, the start of a disinfection process that aims to kill the tiny beetles burrowed into them.
The drugstore beetle, also known as the bread beetle, is often found among dried foodstuffs like grains, flour and spices. But they also are attracted to the gelatin and starch-based adhesives found in books.
Sponsor Message
They have been found in a section of the library housing around a quarter of the abbey's 400,000 volumes.
"This is an advanced insect infestation which has been detected in several parts of the library, so the entire collection is classified as infected and must be treated all at the same time," said Zsófia Edit Hajdu, the chief restorer on the project. "We've never encountered such a degree of infection before."
Abbey houses historical treasures
The beetle invasion was first detected during a routine library cleaning. Employees noticed unusual layers of dust on the shelves and then saw that holes had been burrowed into some of the book spines. Upon opening the volumes, burrow holes could be seen in the paper where the beetles chewed through.
The abbey at Pannonhalma was founded in 996, four years before the establishment of the Kingdom of Hungary. Sitting upon a tall hill in northwestern Hungary, the abbey houses the country's oldest collection of books, as well as many of its earliest and most important written records.
In this photo provided by Pannonhalma Archabbey, a restorer shows an old book with holes in its pages due to a drugstore beetle infestation, at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary on July 3.
AP/Pannonhalma Archabbey
hide caption
toggle caption
AP/Pannonhalma Archabbey
For over 1,000 years, the abbey has been among the most prominent religious and cultural sites in Hungary and all of Central Europe, surviving centuries of wars and foreign incursions such as the Ottoman invasion and occupation of Hungary in the 16th century.
Sponsor Message
Ilona Ásványi, director of the Pannonhalma Archabbey library, said she is "humbled" by the historical and cultural treasures the collection holds whenever she enters.
"It is dizzying to think that there was a library here a thousand years ago, and that we are the keepers of the first book catalogue in Hungary," she said.
Performing Arts
Take a peek at Stephen Sondheim's papers, now at the Library of Congress
Among the library's most outstanding works are 19 codices, including a complete Bible from the 13th century. It also houses several hundred manuscripts predating the invention of the printing press in the mid-15th century and tens of thousands of books from the 16th century.
While the oldest and rarest prints and books are stored separately and have not been infected, Ásványi said any damage to the collection represents a blow to cultural, historical and religious heritage.
"When I see a book chewed up by a beetle or infected in any other way, I feel that no matter how many copies are published and how replaceable the book is, a piece of culture has been lost," she said.
Books will spend weeks in an oxygen-free environment
To kill the beetles, the crates of books are being placed into tall, hermetically sealed plastic sacks from which all oxygen is removed. After six weeks in the pure nitrogen environment, the abbey hopes all the beetles will be destroyed.
Before being reshelved, each book will be individually inspected and vacuumed. Any book damaged by the pests will be set aside for later restoration work.
This photo provided by Pannonhalma Archabbey shows books kept in hermetically sealed plastic sacks for disinfection at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary on July 3 as a beetle infestation threatens its ancient collection.
AP/Pannonhalma Archabbey

data.title: Mushroom learns to crawl after being given robot body (2024)
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了康奈尔大学和佛罗伦萨大学的研究团队开发了一种新型生物混合机器人，利用可食用的King Trumpet蘑菇发出的电信号来移动和感知环境。这种机器人通过将真菌菌丝体与电子设备结合，能够感知和响应环境变化，可能应用于农业等领域，如监测土壤化学成分。该研究发表在《Science Robotics》期刊上，标志着生物混合机器人在未来应用中的巨大潜力。此前，类似实验包括将人工虫脑植入乐高机器人以及麻省理工学院研发的结合活体肌肉组织的机器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：将真菌与机器人技术结合的科学实验及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **对实验中“学习”一词的质疑**：
  - [cloudbonsai] 和 [Legend2440] 都认为用“学习”来描述这个实验是不准确的。他们指出，蘑菇只是被动地根据光信号产生生物信号，机器人根据这个信号触发行动，蘑菇并没有主动学习或控制机器人。
  
• **对生物与机器人结合的兴趣和潜力**：
  - [theflyestpilot] 提到了一部涉及类似概念的动画，并对将真菌与机器人结合表示支持。
  - [lioeters] 认为将生物有机体与机械系统结合具有探索潜力，并举例说明其他类似的实验，如给乌龟滑板和金鱼车辆。

• **对实验伦理的关注**：
  - [paweladamczuk] 提出如果使用老鼠或猫的大脑进行类似实验，可能会引发伦理问题。他幽默地提到，当真菌学会请求食物时，可能就是伦理问题浮现的时刻。

补充讨论：
• **对实验潜在风险的担忧**：
  - [TylerLives] 以反问的形式表达了对实验可能带来的风险的担忧。
  - [chkaloon] 提到流行文化中类似的情节（如《星际迷航》中的菌丝导航情节），暗示对这种技术应用的怀疑。

• **其他相关实验和研究**：
  - [mhuffman] 提供了关于“死灵机器人学”（Necrobotics）的参考资料，展示了一个相关的科学技巧。
  - [accoil] 提供了更多关于康奈尔大学有机机器人实验室的研究链接。
  - [ProfHiggs] 提到黏菌的惊人能力，提供了一篇相关的自然文章。

• **幽默和创意联想**：
  - [adxl] 开玩笑地说未来可能会出现“蘑菇大脑”。
  - [BSOhealth] 以幽默的方式设想了一本“蘑菇自传”，描述了蘑菇在获得灵长类身体后学会建造计算机的情景。

• **文化联想**：
  - [amelius] 提到了一个关于鱼控制车辆的类似研究，提供了相关的参考链接。

争议焦点：
• 实验中蘑菇是否真正“学习”或只是被动响应信号是讨论的主要争议点。一方认为蘑菇只是作为传感器存在，另一方则强调这种结合实验的潜在探索价值和未来可能性。

Your support helps us to tell the story

From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging.
At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story.
The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it.
Your support makes all the difference.
Read more
Engineers have created a new type of
robot
that places living fungi behind the controls.
The
biohybrid robot
uses electrical signals from an edible type of mushroom called a king trumpet in order to move around and sense its environment.
Developed by an interdisciplinary team from Cornell University in the US and Florence University in Italy, the machine could herald a new era of living robotics.
“Living systems respond to touch, they respond to light, they respond to heat, they respond to even some unknowns, like signals,” said Anand Mishra, a research associate in the Organic Robotics Lab at Cornell.
“That’s why we think, OK, if you wanted to build future
robots
, how can they work in an unexpected environment? We can leverage these living systems, and any unknown input comes in, the robot will respond to that.”
Researchers from Cornell University in the US and the University of Florence in Italy placed a species of edible mushroom within a robot body
(
Robert Shepherd
)
Different inputs, such as ultraviolet light, resulted in different outcomes for the way the robot moved. A video of one of the mushroom-controlled robots shows it moving slowly across a surface by pumping its robotic legs. Another biohybrid robot uses a wheeled system in order to move around.
Combining this mobility with the fungi’s ability to sense chemical and biological signals could prove useful in a range of applications, according to the researchers.
“By growing mycelium into the electronics of a robot, we were able to allow the biohybrid machine to sense and respond to the environment,” said Rob Shepherd, a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at Cornell.
“The potential for future robots could be to sense soil chemistry in row crops and decide when to add more fertiliser, for example, perhaps mitigating downstream effects of agriculture like harmful algal blooms.”
Details of the biohybrid robot were published in the journal
Science Robotics
, in
a study
titled ‘Sensorimotor control of robots mediated by electro-physiological measurements of fungal mycelia’.
It is not the first time a living organism has been placed inside a robot body, though the use of mushrooms could offer a major breakthrough in the field of biohybrid robotics due to their ability to grow and survive in harsh conditions.
Previous experiments have included
an artificial worm brain placed inside a Lego robot
, which was able to recreate the creature’s movements and intentions.
Earlier this year, researchers from Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) created a machine that was integrated with living muscle tissue in order to sense and adapt to its environment.

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在Rust中开发FAT文件系统驱动时遇到的特化（specialization）问题，以及如何通过函数指针解决该问题。Rust目前不支持稳定的特化功能，导致无法为只读和读写文件系统分别定义不同的`load_nth_sector`方法实现。作者尝试了多种方法，最终通过使用函数指针实现了类似特化的功能，从而绕开了这一限制。本文强调了在没有特化支持的情况下，如何利用其他Rust特性来实现相似的行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中的特质（trait）特化及其相关问题，如重叠实例、生命周期处理等。

不同观点：
• [hackyhacky] 认为特质特化在此场景中并不合适，建议使用两种替代方案：将文件系统本身作为一个特质，通过不同实现来处理只读和读写情况；或者在文件系统对象中存储能力信息，并在运行时通过条件查询。这些方法可能更简洁和清晰。

• [maybevoid] 提出使用上下文泛型编程（CGP）来绕过一致性限制，通过提供者特质在安全的稳定Rust中实现重叠实现，并提供了一个概念验证实现链接。

• [ozgrakkurt] 建议使用特质对象，通过默认实现和特化来解决问题，认为这种方法比使用宏或增加泛型更简单，并且编译时间更好。

• [SkiFire13] 指出特化功能在处理生命周期时存在问题，特别是当某些类型根据生命周期实现特质时会导致特化不健全，这也是特化功能在稳定化过程中面临的主要障碍。

• [konstantinua00] 提出通过负特质（negative traits）来解决问题，认为可以通过定义负特质来避免特化时重叠检查的问题。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对特质特化的争议主要集中在代码的清晰性、运行时行为、编译时间以及处理特化时出现的生命周期问题。
• 提出了多种替代方案，如使用特质对象、上下文泛型编程和负特质，展示了在Rust中解决特化问题的不同思路。
• 对特化功能在Rust中的稳定性和健全性存在一定担忧，特别是涉及到复杂的生命周期处理时。

44590671.article_content:
"Bypassing" specialization in Rust or How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love Function Pointers
I've spent nearly a year developing and refining my own FAT driver in Rust. For much of the last six months, I had to put the project on hold due to school commitments. However, I'm back now, especially since this project has become my most-starred repository on GitHub. During that journey, I (almost) learned how FAT and filesystems in general work behind-the-scenes and in my attempts to navigate the constraints imposed by the Rust programming language, I encountered what I thought was an immovable obstacle:
specialization
A quick word about specialization
Specialization as a concept was introduced with
RFC 1210
all the way back to 2015, long before I even had a serious passion about computers and programming. For our use case, specialization allows us to essentially override trait and struct
impl
s. Let me demonstrate with an example:
trait
A
{
}
trait
B
{
}
struct
MyStruct
<
S
>
(
S
)
where
S
:
A
;
impl
<
S
>
MyStruct
<
S
>
where
S
:
A
{
fn
do_something
(
&
self
)
{
// do something here
}
}
impl
<
S
>
MyStruct
<
S
>
where
S
:
A
+
B
{
fn
do_something
(
&
self
)
{
// do something else here
}
}
In Rust, the above code wouldn't compile, since we define the function
do_something
twice. With specialization, the compiler would realize that the second
impl
is more "specialized" than the first one and the above code would compile just fine. Then, if we constructed the struct
MyStruct
with its only field containing an object that implements trait
A
but not trait
B
, then we did the same but with an object that now implements both
A
and
B
, and called the
do_something
method on each one struct, the first
do_something
implementation and second
do_something
implementation would be run respectively. Cool, so why do the above code not compile? Well, I am not an expert in Rust soundness and safety, but according to the tracking issue (
#31844
) and some Zulip chats and Rust user forum threads I've found, there's a lifetime-related issue with the whole feature that no one knows how to easily solve. There's another feature,
min-specialization
which seems to not suffer from that problem to the same extent, but its still unstable, and since I don't wanna deal with safety issues and I also would like my project to be on the stable toolchain, that won't suit us.
Why do we need specialization anyways?
That's a good question. It all comes down to how I've come to choose to communicate with the storage device. FAT filesystems are subdivided to sectors, where each sector stores a fixed amount of data, which can be either 512, 1024, 2048 or 4096 bytes (there are also clusters, which are subdivisions of file data and whose size is an integer multiple of the sector size, but we don't care about clusters right now because of what you are gonna read below). Each time we want to read or modify a certain piece of data, we load that sector to a sector buffer, which is just an array, we read our data from the buffer or directly modify them there, and when we want to load another sector, we first sync the buffer back to the filesystem if there are any changes. The issue might not be apparent right now, but it will be in a bit.
To implement a
FileSystem
struct that can be either Read-Only or Read/Write, we should define read-related methods in
impl
blocks that require the storage to support
Read
and
Seek
.
Write
-related methods should be defined in blocks that require
Read
,
Write
, and
Seek
. Let's take a look into our hypothetical function to loads the corresponding sector into the sector buffer.
// struct is defined above
impl
<
S
>
FileSystem
<
S
>
where
S
:
Read
+
Seek
{
fn
load_nth_sector
(
&
mut
self
)
->
Result
<
(
)
,
S
::
Error
>
{
// our logic goes here
}
}
Any functions that performs any kind of read and write function would call this to make sure that the correct sector is in the sector buffer. But this function is within a
Read
+
Seek
impl
block, which means that it can't write to the storage and thus any changes to the sector buffer are never synced back to the storage medium. With specialization we would be able to do the following, which we can't, since specialization as of writing this is an unstable feature:
// struct is defined above
impl
<
S
>
FileSystem
<
S
>
where
S
:
Read
+
Seek
{
fn
load_nth_sector
(
&
mut
self
)
->
Result
<
(
)
,
S
::
Error
>
{
// our read-only logic goes here
}
}
impl
<
S
>
FileSystem
<
S
>
where
S
:
Read
+
Write
+
Seek
{
fn
load_nth_sector
(
&
mut
self
)
->
Result
<
(
)
,
S
::
Error
>
{
// our read-only logic goes here
}
}
Of course Rust complains that the
load_nth_sector
function is defined twice and thus the code above fails to compile.
After procrastinating for quite some time due to this very issue, I then decided to try solving it.
Attempt #1: Check if someone else has "implemented" specialization with a macro of some kind
I eventually stepped upon
spez
(spez stands for specialization if it isn't

data.title: Matterport walkthrough of the original Microsoft Building 3
data.author: uticus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软旧办公环境及相关记忆

不同观点：
• **怀旧与复杂情感**：
  - [avidiax] 和 [ThrowawayB7] 提到早期在微软工作时，员工根据资历可以获得独立办公室，甚至是有窗的办公室。这种环境让他们感到怀念，但也有人提到如今微软已经转向开放式办公室。
  - [mittermayr] 则强调了对微软工作的复杂情感，回忆像快照一样断断续续，既有美好时光，也有难以抓住的细节。

• **办公环境对工作的影响**：
  - [Rodeoclash] 表达了对小型独立办公室的向往，认为这样的设置有助于专注工作，并可以根据个人喜好布置房间。
  - [mynameisash] 提到建筑设计不合理导致迷路的挫折感，尤其是对建筑内部结构的困惑。

• **办公设施与细节**：
  - [canucker2016] 关注办公楼的零食和饮料选择，对饮料种类的减少表示不满，认为选择受限且不适合所有人的口味。
  - [tomcam] 强调了在Building 2工作的美好体验，尤其是自然环境和运动设施带来的便利和愉悦。

补充讨论：
• **历史与技术**：
  - [dreamcompiler] 提到了微软最早的建筑位于阿尔伯克基，并提供了相关链接。
  - [Helithumper] 提供了相关的博客文章链接，进一步探讨微软的旧办公室。
  - [buran77] 提供了办公环境视频的保存方法，方便收藏和存档。

• **对未来技术的展望**：
  - [Aeolun] 和 [jerpint] 提到了对过去办公设计的欣赏，并对未来技术如Gaussian splatting在虚拟环境中的应用表示期待。

• **建筑设计细节**：
  - [dhx] 对办公楼内部使用钢化玻璃的设计目的表示好奇，提出疑问。

• **细节观察**：
  - [jwoglom] 注意到微软的黑色垃圾桶上有公司标识，对此表示了一种特殊的情感。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在微软办公环境从独立办公室向开放式办公室转变的过程，以及这种转变对员工情感和工作效率的影响。

data.title: Erythritol linked to brain cell damage and stroke risk
data.author: OutOfHere
data.article_summary: 一项由科罗拉多大学博尔德分校进行的研究显示，广泛使用的糖替代品——赤藓糖醇，可能并非无害。尽管赤藓糖醇因低热量和不影响胰岛素水平而被推荐给肥胖和糖尿病患者，但新研究发现，即使是少量赤藓糖醇也会损害脑血管细胞，导致血管收缩、血栓形成和炎症，从而增加中风风险。实验中，研究人员用相当于无糖饮料中赤藓糖醇含量的样本处理血管细胞，发现这些细胞的一氧化氮减少，内皮素-1增加，血栓分解能力降低，自由基增多。尽管该研究是在细胞层面进行，但作者建议消费者留意食品标签，控制赤藓糖醇摄入。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于赤藓糖醇对人体健康影响的科学讨论及其相关研究的可靠性

不同观点：
• **[duffpkg]** 认为该研究是在细胞培养中进行的，不能直接用于指导人类健康行为。文章中的一些结论缺乏研究支持，读者应查看实际研究。
• **[jcynix]** 指出赤藓糖醇天然存在于一些水果和发酵食品中，因此实验室中使用的剂量可能远高于正常饮食中的摄入量，质疑实验的真实性。
• **[mediumsmart]** 讽刺地表示，只有那些已经存在健康问题的人才会考虑饮用含糖饮料或使用甜味剂，暗示这些行为本身就不健康。
• **[aeze]** 提到自己对赤藓糖醇过敏，并指出该甜味剂在食品中越来越常见，提醒大家注意。
• **[MichealCodes]** 表示自己长期大量摄入赤藓糖醇，询问应该注意哪些健康指标，特别是血压。
• **[IcyWindows]** 对实验中的剂量提出质疑，认为实验中使用的剂量可能不符合实际情况。
• **[Eisenstein]** 详细分析了Witkowski等人（2023）的研究，指出其研究对象多为心血管疾病患者，且未考虑体内自然产生的赤藓糖醇，认为研究结果不可靠。同时提到Khafagy等人（2024）的研究与之矛盾，后者未发现赤藓糖醇增加心血管代谢疾病的风险。
• **[westurner]** 引用了关于β-环糊精（一种糖醇）的研究，指出其可能对动脉粥样硬化有逆转作用，并提到赤藓糖醇作为糖醇的一种，可能与这些研究有相关性。
• **[mixwpl0j]** 质疑那些选择用化学甜味剂代替天然糖的人的健康状态，暗示这些人可能本身健康状况不佳。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于赤藓糖醇的安全性及其在食品中的广泛使用，特别是在心血管健康方面的影响。
• 一些评论者（如Eisenstein）对研究方法和对象的选择提出质疑，认为研究结果不能直接推广到普通人群。
• 其他评论者（如aeze和MichealCodes）关注个体对赤藓糖醇的敏感性和长期摄入可能带来的健康风险。
• 讨论中还涉及对天然存在于食物中的赤藓糖醇与人工添加的赤藓糖醇之间剂量和效果的比较。

44621268.article_content:
Science News
from research organizations
Popular sugar substitute linked to brain cell damage and stroke risk
Study suggests the sweetener erythritol, often recommended for people with obesity and diabetes, may come with health risks of its own
Date:
July 19, 2025
Source:
University of Colorado at Boulder
Summary:
Erythritol, a widely used sugar substitute found in many low-carb and sugar-free products, may not be as harmless as once believed. New research from the University of Colorado Boulder reveals that even small amounts of erythritol can harm brain blood vessel cells, promoting constriction, clotting, and inflammation—all of which may raise the risk of stroke.
Share:
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
LinkedIN
Email
FULL STORY
Even small amounts of erythritol may trigger harmful changes in brain blood vessels, potentially raising stroke risk. Credit: Shutterstock
From low-carb ice cream to keto protein bars to "sugar-free" soda, the decades-old sweetener erythritol is everywhere.
But new University of Colorado Boulder research shows the popular sugar substitute and specialty food additive comes with serious downsides, impacting brain cells in numerous ways that can boost risk of stroke.
The study was published in the
Journal of Applied Physiology
.
"Our study adds to the evidence suggesting that non-nutritive sweeteners that have generally been purported to be safe, may not come without negative health consequences," said senior author Christopher DeSouza, professor of integrative physiology and director of the Integrative Vascular Biology Lab.
First approved by the Food and Drug Administration in 2001, erythritol is a sugar alcohol, often produced by fermenting corn and found in hundreds of products. It has almost no calories, is about 80% as sweet as table sugar, and has negligible impact on insulin levels, making it a favorite for people trying to lose weight, keep their blood sugar in check or avoid carbohydrates.
But recent research has begun to shed light on its risks.
One recent study involving 4,000 people in the U.S. and Europe found that men and women with higher circulating levels of erythritol were significantly more likely to have a heart attack or stroke within the next three years.
DeSouza and first author Auburn Berry, a graduate student in his lab, set out to understand what might be driving that increased risk.
Researchers in the lab treated human cells that line blood vessels in the brain for three hours with about the same amount of erythritol contained in a typical sugar-free beverage.
They observed that the treated cells were altered in numerous ways: They expressed significantly less nitric oxide, a molecule that relaxes and widens blood vessels, and more endothelin-1, a protein that constricts blood vessels. Meanwhile, when challenged with a clot-forming compound called thrombin, cellular production of the natural clot-busting compound t-PA was "markedly blunted." The erythritol-treated cells also produced more reactive oxygen species (ROS), a.k.a. "free radicals," metabolic byproducts which can age and damage cells and inflame tissue.
"Big picture, if your vessels are more constricted and your ability to break down blood clots is lowered, your risk of stroke goes up," said Berry. "Our research demonstrates not only that, but how erythritol has the potential to increase stroke risk."
DeSouza notes that their study used only a serving-size worth of the sugar substitute. For those who consume multiple servings per day, the impact, presumably, could be worse.
The authors caution that their study was a laboratory study, conducted on cells, and larger studies in people are needed.
That said, De Souza encourages consumers to read labels, looking for erythritol or "sugar alcohol" on the label.
"Given the epidemiological study that inspired our work, and now our cellular findings, we believe it would be prudent for people to monitor their consumption of non-nutrient-sweeteners such as this one," he said.

44621268.article_summary: 一项由科罗拉多大学博尔德分校进行的研究显示，广泛使用的糖替代品——赤藓糖醇，可能并非无害。尽管赤藓糖醇因低热量和不影响胰岛素水平而被推荐给肥胖和糖尿病患者，但新研究发现，即使是少量赤藓糖醇也会损害脑血管细胞，导致血管收缩、血栓形成和炎症，从而增加中风风险。实验中，研究人员用相当于无糖饮料中赤藓糖醇含量的样本处理血管细胞，发现这些细胞的一氧化氮减少，内皮素-1增加，血栓分解能力降低，自由基增多。尽管该研究是在细胞层面进行，但作者建议消费者留意食品标签，控制赤藓糖醇摄入。
44621268.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于赤藓糖醇对人体健康影响的科学讨论及其相关研究的可靠性

不同观点：
• **[duffpkg]** 认为该研究是在细胞培养中进行的，不能直接用于指导人类健康行为。文章中的一些结论缺乏研究支持，读者应查看实际研究。
• **[jcynix]** 指出赤藓糖醇天然存在于一些水果和发酵食品中，因此实验室中使用的剂量可能远高于正常饮食中的摄入量，质疑实验的真实性。
• **[mediumsmart]** 讽刺地表示，只有那些已经存在健康问题的人才会考虑饮用含糖饮料或使用甜味剂，暗示这些行为本身就不健康。
• **[aeze]** 提到自己对赤藓糖醇过敏，并指出该甜味剂在食品中越来越常见，提醒大家注意。
• **[MichealCodes]** 表示自己长期大量摄入赤藓糖醇，询问应该注意哪些健康指标，特别是血压。
• **[IcyWindows]** 对实验中的剂量提出质疑，认为实验中使用的剂量可能不符合实际情况。
• **[Eisenstein]** 详细分析了Witkowski等人（2023）的研究，指出其研究对象多为心血管疾病患者，且未考虑体内自然产生的赤藓糖醇，认为研究结果不可靠。同时提到Khafagy等人（2024）的研究与之矛盾，后者未发现赤藓糖醇增加心血管代谢疾病的风险。
• **[westurner]** 引用了关于β-环糊精（一种糖醇）的研究，指出其可能对动脉粥样硬化有逆转作用，并提到赤藓糖醇作为糖醇的一种，可能与这些研究有相关性。
• **[mixwpl0j]** 质疑那些选择用化学甜味剂代替天然糖的人的健康状态，暗示这些人可能本身健康状况不佳。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于赤藓糖醇的安全性及其在食品中的广泛使用，特别是在心血管健康方面的影响。
• 一些评论者（如Eisenstein）对研究方法和对象的选择提出质疑，认为研究结果不能直接推广到普通人群。
• 其他评论者（如aeze和MichealCodes）关注个体对赤藓糖醇的敏感性和长期摄入可能带来的健康风险。
• 讨论中还涉及对天然存在于食物中的赤藓糖醇与人工添加的赤藓糖醇之间剂量和效果的比较。

data.title: I Used Arch, BTW: macOS, Day 1
data.author: yberreby
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了他从使用九年的Arch Linux转向Apple M4 Pro MacBook Pro的经历。他详细描述了在新MacBook上配置环境以适应日常工作需求的过程，特别针对从Linux转向Apple Silicon的用户。作者是麦吉尔大学的神经AI研究博士生，工作流包括阅读和注释科学论文、使用Zed编辑器编码、管理Python项目、运行深度学习实验等。他回顾了使用Arch Linux的优点，如包管理优秀、系统高度可定制等，但也提到硬件问题促使他转向MacBook。文章为考虑从Linux切换到Mac的用户提供了参考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕macOS、Linux以及Homebrew等工具的优缺点展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• [w10-1] 认为没有必要将macOS改造成Arch，建议直接在macOS上使用虚拟机运行Arch，并指出Apple的虚拟化框架性能良好，但存在一些限制如图形支持不足。同时提到M4处理器的性能优势，特别是在CPU追踪功能上的独特性。

• [Sytten] 抱怨Homebrew在安装软件时会引发一系列不必要的依赖和更新问题，导致虚拟环境被破坏。

• [jasoneckert] 支持Linux系统，但在Apple Silicon上使用Fedora Asahi Remix，认为其运行速度远快于macOS。

• [disintegrator] 提出使用静态二进制文件和mise工具管理开发工具，以避免Homebrew和Nix的复杂性。

• [moribvndvs] 对macOS逐渐失去其原有的用户自由和可靠性感到不满，并对Apple将其转变为类似iOS的封闭系统表示担忧。

• [st3fan] 作为Homebrew的长期用户，否认Homebrew会导致系统依赖关系破裂的说法，认为这是个别现象。

• [mmcnl] 对macBook Pro与便宜的Asus笔记本的比较不以为然，认为与高端的Lenovo或HP笔记本相比，macOS并没有明显的优势。

• [bee_rider] 对Apple芯片的性能表示赞赏，但认为AMD的APU也有其优势，可以在x86架构上停留更久。

• [seec] 指出高价的Apple电脑与廉价笔记本的比较并不公平，认为高价产品理应表现更好。

• [Szpadel] 通过在Linux机器上调整CPU调度器解决了UI卡顿问题，认为其Linux机器运行比M1 mini更流畅。

• [xelxebar] 刚购买了M4 Air，对从Linux转向macOS可能带来的工作流摩擦表示担忧，并询问nixos-darwin与虚拟机的比较以及是否有必要折腾Apple的启动引导。

• [Liquix] 建议使用yabai和sketchybar来实现i3/hyprland风格的平铺窗口管理，适合终端工作流。

• [fernandojose] 使用Arch和macOS的经验兼有，偏爱Arch的pacman包管理器，但对macOS上的Homebrew没有太大问题。

• [SanjayMehta] 在日常工作中使用macOS，但严肃工作在Linux工作站上进行，强调硬件成本低于时间成本。

• [bigyabai] 认为Nix在macOS上的表现很差，远不如在NixOS上的原生体验。

补充讨论：
• 对Homebrew和Nix的复杂性与系统破坏风险的不同看法。
• 对Apple Silicon硬件性能的认可与对其封闭性的批评。
• 对Linux在Apple Silicon上的表现及其配置灵活性的讨论。
• 对高价Apple设备与廉价设备的性价比比较。

争议焦点：
• macOS与Linux在开发工作流中的优劣比较。
• Homebrew和Nix在包管理上的复杂性与可靠性问题。
• Apple Silicon硬件的高性能与封闭性之间的平衡。

44620623.article_content:
Contents
TL;DR
:
I used Arch Linux for nine years as a daily driver on non-Apple laptops.
I received my new M4 Pro MacBook Pro yesterday.
This recounts my experience configuring it to hit the ground running from day 1.
If you're a Linux user making the switch to Apple Silicon, or thinking of doing so, this post may be of interest.
Zed
,
AeroSpace
,
Raycast
's "Switch Windows" and
Alacritty
in action.
What I Need My Computer For
The way one uses their computer is shaped by their needs, values, and habits.
As of writing, I am midway through my PhD at McGill University and
Mila
, focusing on neuro-AI research at
McGill's Department of Physiology
.
My background is in computer engineering.
My workflow as a PhD student involves a mix of:
Filing, reading and annotating scientific papers using
Zotero
;
Writing code in
Zed
, a fast text editor with first-class support for
LSP and Tree-Sitter
, GPU acceleration,
Rust-powered multithreading
, and, non-negotiably,
vim bindings
;
Doing most of my computer interaction inside of a
zsh
shell with a featureful prompt such as
Starship
(previously,
grml-zsh-config
or
oh-my-zsh
);
Managing Python projects using Astral's
uv
;
Writing bespoke command-line utilities in
Rust
;
Using
JAX
and
PyTorch
for numerical simulations and deep (reinforcement) learning;
Doing exploratory development using local
Jupyter Lab
notebooks
1
;
Firing off longer-running jobs on remote compute resources, using on-premises workstations or larger
SLURM
clusters;
Writing down notes in my
org-roam
personal knowledge base;
Writing papers and slides in
Typst
or LaTeX (if I have to);
Collaborating with colleagues on
Zulip
, Slack, or in person;
Attending scientific meetings in-person or virtually (and taking live notes in org-roam);
Staring intensely at a whiteboard/wall/ceiling when I'm mulling over a problem (no tech required);
Debugging anything and everything: driver issues on compute workstations, sub-millisecond timing code in
psychophysics
experiments using custom
Teensy
photodiode contraptions, shared object loading in
proprietary camera software
, etc.
Writing blog posts such as this one using a static site generator,
Zola
.
Depending on the needs of the hour, I'll put on my researcher, engineer, sysadmin, or communicator hat, and I need my computing environment to support this workflow.
Nine Beautiful Years of Arch Linux
I didn't start out on Linux.
I digitally grew up on
System 7
,
Mac OS 9
, then
Mac OS X
, in an Apple-centric household where "Windows" was a profanity.
While the UNIX backbone of Mac OS X made it a great introduction to computing, I eventually grew frustrated with the developer experience, exorbitant repair costs (what do you mean, everything is glued or soldered?), lackluster GPU performance, and poor support for projects I wanted to hack on.
As a result, I switched to
Arch Linux
in 2016 after briefly trying Debian, Ubuntu, and Fedora.
Since then, I've faithfully used Arch as my daily driver on various machines: a trusty
Asus Zenbook UX410U
, two self-built desktop workstations, numerous VirtualBox VMs, two Tuxedo Pulse 15 laptops from
Tuxedo Computers
, an Asus TUF A15, and others.
After a couple of early reinstalls, I mostly migrated systems via SSD swaps or
dd
clones.
From day one, I embraced the Arch spirit, consistently running either
i3
or
sway
as my tiling window managers of choice, complete with a panel of shortcuts allowing me to get much of my computer use done at the speed of thought. I'm proud to say that over the years, a number of friends and coworkers adopted similar setups after seeing how fast one's computer use could get, in search of a streamlined yet ruthlessly efficient system configuration.
Arch is a stellar distro.
The package management story is top-notch.
Packages are up-to-date, easy to create and maintain, and come close to the upstream sources without distro-specific patches.
pacman
just works, and the
AUR
gives you access to the most obscure of packages.
The documentation on the
Arch Wiki
is excellent, to the point that it's often worth checking when troubleshooting a problem on another distro.
On Arch, you build your system piece by piece, trading initial setup time for deep understanding.
This is both intellectually satisfying and practically empowering.
Given how freeing the Arch experience is, it has been difficult for me to imagine using anything else.
Occasionally having to use a Mac or Windows PC seemed like a test of patience; Arch felt like
home
.
A computing environment that I trust, that I understand, built by and for me, sculpted according to my precise needs, changing by my will and not due to some tech company's idea of what's good for me ("hey, it's 2025, we should
make everything unreadable!
").
So... what's the catch, then?
Why migrate away from something so good?
Hardware That Wears You Out
While Arch Linux itself, as a Linux distribution, is great, it needs to run on
something
.
And when it comes to laptops, that
something
is not g

data.title: How to run an Arduino for years on a battery (2021)
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了如何通过优化硬件和软件，让Arduino系统在电池供电下运行多年。通常Arduino由USB供电，但在自主项目中需要电池供电，直接使用Arduino板如Uno R3会快速耗尽电池。为了延长电池寿命，需要自行构建最小硬件系统，并优化软件以降低功耗。

**硬件方面**，使用ATMega328微控制器、少量电容、电阻、LED、晶振等组件，直接用电池供电，避免使用耗电的电压调节器。通过面包板和跳线连接电路。

**软件方面**，利用Arduino IDE编程，使用JeeLib库让系统进入低功耗睡眠模式，只在需要时唤醒，从而最大限度节省电力。文章提供了硬件连接步骤和示例代码，帮助实现低功耗Arduino系统。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [_ache_]: 指出代码中的明显错误，即 `#include <JeeLib.h;>`，并质疑该库的文档质量，认为其看起来像被废弃的项目，且可能遭遇了域名抢注或品牌劫持。他对项目的可靠性和维护状态持怀疑态度。

• [icedrop]: 提出图片加载问题，表示图片无法正常显示，可能影响其对评论或项目的理解。这是一个技术问题，与讨论的核心内容不直接相关，但影响了讨论体验。

• [whatever1]: 提出是否存在专门用于高效休眠和唤醒其他微控制器的微控制器。这个观点探讨了特定硬件在低功耗管理方面的可能性，暗示可能有更优的硬件解决方案。

• [xmprt]: 认为在实际复杂项目中，低功耗模式的管理并不简单。他举例说明了一个需要保持WiFi连接、接收传感器信号并管理多线程的项目场景，强调在这种情境下，低功耗模式的管理会变得复杂，不是简单的循环就能解决。

• [ggm]: 讨论了使用RF（如WiFi或BT）对功耗的影响，提到固定点采样和时钟漂移问题。他还提到了使用类似Morse码的脉冲干扰技术来唤醒设备，并引用了Zigbee和6lowpan等技术。他认为通过LED闪烁传递信息也是一种远程读取方式，并提到了历史上的一些技术应用（如Newton的IR网络）。

• 争议焦点：_ache_对项目是否被废弃及品牌问题的质疑与其他技术讨论形成对比，表明对项目可靠性的担忧。
• 复杂项目中的低功耗管理：xmprt和ggm都提到了在复杂项目中实现低功耗的困难，涉及WiFi连接、传感器唤醒和多线程管理等问题。
• 硬件与技术的选择：whatever1和ggm都提到了特定的硬件（如微控制器）和技术（如Zigbee、6lowpan、IR网络）在低功耗项目中的应用，暗示不同的项目需求可能需要不同的解决方案。

44590391.article_content:
How to Run an Arduino for Years on a Battery
June 17, 2021
â¢
15 min read
If you found this article after doing a search on Google, welcome! On this website you will find plenty of content around DIY home automation using open-source hardware. Enjoy the article!
For most of the Arduino tutorials you will find on this website, power is usually not an issue as the Arduino is powered by the USB cable coming from the computer. However, sometimes you want to build systems that are going to be autonomous and powered by a battery.
For example, you want to power a wireless motion detector just by using a set of batteries. The first idea would be to connect directly an Arduino board like the Arduino Uno R3 to a battery. Easy, right ? Well, it would work, but your battery would be depleted in a matter of days because some components like voltage regulators are always sucking power. So we need something better.
The first thing we need is to build our own Arduino system with just the minimal set of components. The second part is to optimise the software so that the system only consumes power when it is actually doing something. And thatâs exactly what we will see in this article.
Hardware & Software Requirements
You need several components to build you own Arduino system. The main piece of this project is of course the microcontroller that will run your Arduino sketches, like the
ATMega328
. You will need a chip with the Arduino bootloader. Buy your chip with it, it will make your life easier.
In a previous project I used a
FTDI breakout board
to program the Arduino chip directly on the breadboard. But for this project I wonât have any external power running on the breadboard so I will just use an Arduino Uno board to program the microcontroller.
To power the Arduino, you will need a battery. The best is to power the Arduino directly from the battery, so you donât have to use any voltage regulators that will suck some power. I used a
set of two AA batteries
(1.5V each) with a
battery holder
thus powering the microcontroller with around 3V, which is fine according to the
ATmega328 documentation
.
You will also need several components around the chip. You will need
one 10uF capacitor
,
two 22pF capacitors
,
one 10K Ohm resistor
,
one 220 Ohm resistor
,
one green LED
, and one
16MHz crystal clock
.
Finally, you will need a
breadboard and some jumper wires
.
This is the list of the components that were used in this article:
Atmel ATmega328
10uF capacitor
Two 22pF capacitors
10K Ohm resistor
220 Ohm resistor
One green LED
16MHz crystal clock
Battery holder
2 AA batteries
Breadboard and some jumper wires
On the software side, you just need the usual Arduino IDE. Note that in this tutorial, we will only cover a tiny part of the possibilities offered by the Arduino platform.
Hardware Configuration
This project is a bit complex to build, so be sure to follow the instructions. This is how it should look like at the end:
First, put the microcontroller in the center of the breadboard. You can then take care about the power: connect power lines on each side, connect the negative power rail to the two GND pins of the microcontroller, and the positive power rail to VCC, AVCC, and AREF. Also, add the 10uF capacitor between two power rails. Finally, add the battery to the system.
You also have to add the crystal between the X1 and X2 pins, with 22pF capacitors going from each pin to the ground. Also, you need to connect the RST pin to the positive power rail using a 10K Ohm resistor. To see if the system is working, connect the green LED in series with a 220 Ohm resistor to the digital pin 13 of the Arduino board, the other side going to the ground.
This is the complete schematics of the project:
Testing your Arduino system
Itâs now time to test if the hardware part is working. What I did in this project is to use the Arduino Uno board to program the chip, and then I just âtransplantedâ the chip on the breadboard. You can just use the default âblinkâ sketch to program the microcontroller. After this is done, just replace the chip on the breadboard, and plug your battery (my battery pack even has a nice on/off switch). The LED should just goes on and off every second as expected.
Optimizing for Low-power
So now, we have an autonomous Arduino system. But it still consuming way too much power. Indeed, even when the LED is off, the Arduino chip is still active and consumes power. But there are functions on the microcontroller to put it to sleep during the time it is inactive, and re-activate the chip when we need to change the state of an output or to perform some measurements. I tested many solutions to really reduce the power to the lowest value possible, and the best I found is the
JeeLib library
. You can just
download it
and install it by placing the folder in your Arduino/libraries/ folder.
This is the sketch I used:
#include <JeeLib.h;>
ISR(WDT_vect) { Sleepy::watchdogEvent(); }
Sleepy::loseSomeTime(5000);

这篇文章介绍了如何通过优化硬件和软件，让Arduino系统在电池供电下运行多年。通常Arduino由USB供电，但在自主项目中需要电池供电，直接使用Arduino板如Uno R3会快速耗尽电池。为了延长电池寿命，需要自行构建最小硬件系统，并优化软件以降低功耗。

**硬件方面**，使用ATMega328微控制器、少量电容、电阻、LED、晶振等组件，直接用电池供电，避免使用耗电的电压调节器。通过面包板和跳线连接电路。

data.title: Borg – Deduplicating archiver with compression and encryption
data.author: rubyn00bie
data.article_summary: BorgBackup（简称Borg）是一款支持重复数据删除、压缩和加密的开源备份工具。它提供高效的存储空间利用，支持安全的身份认证加密，以及多种压缩算法（如lz4、zstd、zlib、lzma或无压缩）。通过FUSE可以挂载备份，便于浏览和恢复数据。Borg易于在多个平台上安装，如Linux、macOS和BSD等，并且采用BSD许可，拥有活跃的开源社区支持。定期检查备份以确保数据安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：备份工具的选择与比较（主要包括Restic、Borg、Kopia等）

不同观点：
• **支持Restic**：
   - **易用性和设置简单**：thangngoc89和kachapopow提到Restic在易用性和设置方面表现更好，尤其是搭配Backrest WebUI或borgmatic时。Kachapopow特别强调Restic的“设置后忘记”特性，减少了对备份失败的担忧。
   - **跨平台支持**：thangngoc89指出Restic支持Windows，并且具备跨机器的去重功能和良好的压缩支持。

• **支持Borg**：
   - **可靠性和性能**：sunaookami和rollcat对Borg的性能和去重功能表示认可，尤其是对服务器和笔记本备份的场景。Rollcat提到自己使用Borg已有约10年，认为其非常出色。
   - **开源社区和作者**：blablabla123提到在一次会议上遇到Borg的作者，并表示作者对数据损坏问题的处理方式让人觉得Borg可靠。
   - **传统与广泛使用**：rjh29认为Borg历史悠久、流行且经过实战检验，特别适合对数据备份要求高的场景。

• **其他工具的提及**：
   - **Kopia**：evulhotdog推荐Kopia，认为其功能与Restic和Borg相似，并且拥有出色的GUI。
   - **Vorta GUI**：jszymborski和ElectronBadger提到使用Vorta作为Borg的GUI前端，解决了Borg命令行操作的不便问题，并且与Hetzner的Storage Box服务兼容良好。
   - **Baqpaq**：dxs提到Baqpaq，它结合了BorgBackup、RSync和RClone，适用于Linux系统，但个人使用基于Tar的自定义脚本。
   - **Plakar**：johng提到Plakar是一个新兴的备份项目，值得关注。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：
   - **Restic vs. Borg**：kachapopow认为Restic在易用性和设置上优于Borg，但rjh29则强调Borg的可靠性和经过时间考验的特性。
   - **备份工具的选择**：AnonC提到正在寻找一种低成本、易用且 robust 的NAS备份方案，尤其是对个人数据隐私有高要求的场景。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**：
   - **加密与去重**：toenail指出，在加密情况下，去重功能仅在每台主机上有效。
   - **工具的性能问题**：jszymborski分享了从Duplicati切换到Borg和Vorta的经历，因为Duplicati在恢复时速度极慢。

总结来看，讨论主要围绕Restic和Borg的比较展开，参与者根据各自的体验和需求支持不同的工具，同时也提及了Kopia、Baqpaq和Plakar等其他备份解决方案。

Backed by a large and active open source community.

data.title: Airbnb allowed rampant price gouging following L.A. fires, city attorney alleges
data.author: miguelazo
data.article_summary: 洛杉矶市检察官Hydee Feldstein Soto办公室起诉Airbnb，指控其在1月山火灾后允许非法抬高房价及存在虚假房东和地址。诉讼要求永久禁止Airbnb在紧急状态下抬高价格，并赔偿受影响消费者。检察官办公室称，Airbnb的验证流程不足，导致用户面临身份盗窃等风险。Airbnb否认指控，称已为火灾恢复提供近3000万美元援助。诉讼还指出，Airbnb上的某些房东使用假名，地址与实际位置相差达四英里。如价格欺诈属实，Airbnb可能违反加州不正当竞争法和反价格欺诈法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Airbnb等平台在突发事件期间的价格上涨问题及其合理性

不同观点：
• jedberg：认为算法定价在突发事件（如需求激增或供应受限）时容易失控，导致价格飙升。平台需要在事后进行调整以防止类似情况。同时指出，有些人对价格不敏感，愿意支付高价以满足需求。难点在于如何找到平衡。
• vouaobrasil：质疑文章未明确价格上涨是由Airbnb本身还是房主引起，并希望看到具体的价格对比例子。
• whatever1：分享了Lyft平台在交通拥堵时价格飙升的亲身经历，指出乘客支付的高价与司机实际收入之间的差距。
• aurareturn：认为无论价格上涨是由Airbnb还是房主引起，都没有问题。价格上涨能激励更多房主出租空置房屋，增加供应。人为压低价格反而不利于无家可归者。
• VarFarYonder：认为这是基本的供需关系，而非恶意涨价，但接受这一点意味着没有人需要为此负责。
• Ccecil：将此问题与“拥堵定价”相比较，认为在资本主义社会中，这种价格波动是正常的。
• exabrial：支持自由市场决定价格，认为过多的监管只会巩固平台的垄断地位。
• baron816：指出住房供应比想象中更具弹性，高价格能激励人们出租闲置空间，且这种影响是边际的，而非全有或全无。

补充讨论：
• rcpt：指出火灾影响了一些美国最富裕地区的房屋，导致大量富人进入短期租赁市场，从而推高价格。
• diziet：提供Airbnb收费约16%的费用信息，为平台收费结构提供背景信息。
• tropicalfruit：对Airbnb将房主称为“host”而非“寄生虫”表示不满，暗示对房主借机涨价的不满。

争议焦点：
• 价格上涨的合理性：一部分人认为这是供需关系的自然结果，另一部分人则质疑平台或房主的道德责任。
• 平台的角色和责任：讨论中涉及到平台是否应对价格波动进行干预，以及干预的最佳方式。
• 自由市场与监管：有人支持自由市场决定价格，反对人为干预，也有人认为需要保护消费者利益。

L.A. City Atty. Hydee Feldstein Soto’s office accused Airbnb of allowing illegal price hikes following the January firestorm. The platform denies the allegations.

The Los Angeles city attorney’s office has filed a lawsuit against Airbnb, accusing the home-sharing platform of allowing price gouging and unverified hosts and addresses at more than 2,000 rentals following the January firestorm in Altadena and Pacific Palisades.
In a statement, L.A. City Atty. Hydee Feldstein Soto’s office accused Airbnb of allowing illegal rental price hikes and permitting false and nonexistent hosts and addresses on the platform. The lawsuit seeks a permanent order to halt Airbnb from hiking up prices during the existing state of emergency, as well as reimbursement for consumers who were charged higher rates.
“Although Airbnb subsequently took steps to curtail price gouging, evidence indicates that illegal gouging on the site continues and may be ongoing,” Feldstein Soto said in a statement announcing the civil enforcement action. “Airbnb is aware that its verification processes are inadequate … potentially luring prospective tenants into a false sense of security about its hosts and locations.”
Advertisement
Airbnb disputed the lawsuit’s accusations, saying the platform has played a consistent role in supporting victims with financial aid following the wildfires.
California
For Subscribers
Scams, bidding wars and predatory landlords: One couple’s quest for housing after the fires
When his Altadena home burned, Todd Smoyer was thrust into a desperate house hunt alongside thousands of other families. He finally found a home, but there were plenty of obstacles along the way.
Feb. 7, 2025
“Since the wildfires broke out, Airbnb … contributed nearly $30 million to fire recovery efforts in Los Angeles, including free emergency housing to nearly 24,000 people impacted by the fires,” an Airbnb spokesperson told The Times. “We will continue supporting the city of Los Angeles in its recovery and rebuilding efforts.”
The lawsuit seeks fines of $2,500 for each instance of alleged price gouging in L.A., which could reach between 2,000 and 3,000 properties, or up to $7.5 million in total penalties.
Advertisement
The lawsuit also alleges that Airbnb’s “inadequate” verification processes left users vulnerable to offenses such as identity theft, robbery, sexual assault, invasion of privacy and voyeurism. Airbnb did not respond to an inquiry from The Times regarding those claims.
The unverified and “nonexistent” hosts alleged in the lawsuit refer to cases of hosts using fake names to represent themselves on the platform.
According to the lawsuit, cases include a profile under the name of “Amber Hiller” that actually belonged to a woman named Akila Nourollah, and a host named “Greg,” verified using the ID of someone named Guven Sacikarali, a relative of the actual account controller, Ali Sacikaral.
Advertisement
California
While many were helped, some fire victims say Airbnb’s free vouchers are useless
More than 100,000 people applied for Airbnb.org’s free housing program, which offers credit to use on Airbnb rentals. But some fire victims who received the vouchers claim they’re useless.
Jan. 29, 2025
While not the correct name of the account owners, Airbnb does allow the use of “preferred names” in its
terms and conditions.
The lawsuit also mentions several cases in which verified locations on Airbnb were actually located up to four miles away from the advertised address.
If price gouging claims are determined to be true, the lawsuit claims that Airbnb can be found to have violated the state’s Unfair Competition Law, California Penal Code Section 396, the Anti-Gouging Law, and the Jan. 16
state of emergency
declaration by Gov. Gavin Newsom, which states that it would be illegal for Airbnb to increase the pricing of rentals by more than 10% during the state of emergency.
The firestorm that erupted on Jan. 7 ultimately destroyed more than 16,000 buildings in Pacific Palisades, Malibu and Altadena.

After disasters, the Federal Emergency Management Agency directly leases apartments for survivors. Despite the horrific housing market in L.A., officials say that isn’t needed here.
May 1, 2025
In January, Airbnb released a statement denouncing price gouging and promising to make it impossible for hosts to raise the prices of their properties by more than 10% from their pre-wildfire rates.

• exabrial：支持自由市场决定价格，认为过多的监管只会巩固平台的垄断地位。
• baron816：指出住房供应比想象中更具弹性，高价格能激励人们出租闲置空间，且这种影响是边际的，而非全有或全无。

补充讨论：
• rcpt：指出火灾影响了一些美国最富裕地区的房屋，导致大量富人进入短期租赁市场，从而推高价格。
• diziet：提供Airbnb收费约16%的费用信息，为平台收费结构提供背景信息。
• tropicalfruit：对Airbnb将房主称为“host”而非“寄生虫”表示不满，暗示对房主借机涨价的不满。

争议焦点：
• 价格上涨的合理性：一部分人认为这是供需关系的自然结果，另一部分人则质疑平台或房主的道德责任。
• 平台的角色和责任：讨论中涉及到平台是否应对价格波动进行干预，以及干预的最佳方式。
• 自由市场与监管：有人支持自由市场决定价格，反对人为干预，也有人认为需要保护消费者利益。

data.author: simonebrunozzi

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：超音速旅行的可行性、经济性及其社会和环境影响

不同观点：
• **超音速旅行的经济性与实用性**：[Y_Y] 认为协和飞机的经济失败主要是由于其噪音问题，而非政府过度监管。超音速旅行在经济上不划算，且噪音令人不适。
• **时间节约的讨论**：[MichaelRazum] 提出，即使超音速飞行节省了飞行时间，大部分时间依然消耗在机场等待上。如果能缩短到达机场的时间，将更有效率。
• **超音速旅行的未来定位**：[Animats] 认为超音速商务飞机可能仅作为富豪的地位象征，而未来的超高速旅行可能更多依赖于视频会议等技术。
• **对高速度的需求质疑**：[namuol] 提出高速度旅行并不符合大众需求，建议发展高铁更为实际，并质疑超音速旅行为谁服务。
• **环境与社会公平问题**：[juujian] 批评超音速旅行是超富人群消耗资源、增加温室气体排放的手段，而普通人的生活质量并未改善。[appreciatorBus] 补充，讨论超音速旅行的经济性和效率时不能忽略外部性（如环境影响）。
• **全球化与地缘政治影响**：[areoform] 持积极态度，认为超音速旅行将极大缩短全球距离，甚至改变地缘政治格局，促进全球和平和跨国创新合作。
• **技术与安全顾虑**：[zeristor] 提到协和飞机曾发生事故，暗示安全问题可能是阻碍超音速技术发展的原因之一。[daft_pink] 指出，现有行业巨头对超音速技术兴趣不大，可能源于对技术风险或市场需求的顾虑。
• **可持续性与舒适性优先**：[jMyles] 认为未来更可能发展的是超舒适且可持续的慢速旅行，而非追求极速。
• **技术细节与误解**：[pfdietz] 指出讨论中混淆了推进剂和燃料的区别，强调液氧成本远低于碳氢燃料，认为这是对超音速飞行经济性讨论中的一个误解。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于超音速旅行的经济性、实用性及其对环境和社会公平的潜在负面影响。支持者认为其能带来地缘政治和全球化的巨大变革，而反对者则关注其成本效益比、环境代价以及服务对象的局限性。

data.title: The AGI Final Frontier: The CLJ-AGI Benchmark
data.author: raspasov
data.article_summary: 文章提出了一种新的AGI（通用人工智能） benchmark，称为CLJ-AGI。其标准是当AI系统能够根据给定要求改进或创建一种编程语言时，即达到AGI。具体要求包括：采用transducer-first设计，消除或选择性保留懒惰求值；尽可能广泛使用协议以提升性能；使一流的数据结构/类型也成为CRDT数据类型以确保正确性和性能；同时增加一流的maps、vectors、arrays、sets、counters等数据结构。成功保持与现有Clojure语言的向后兼容性将获得特别奖励。最终输出是一种新的或改进的编程语言。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AGI（通用人工智能）的能力及其在实际任务中的应用

不同观点：
• [kelseyfrog] 认为，AI研究人员通过基准测试来推动问题解决。只要将问题转化为AGI基准，AI研究人员最终会解决这些问题。这种非正式的分布式计算形式能够产生解决方案和工具，解决复杂的问题。
• [mdemare] 提出两个AGI的最终前沿测试例子，包括重新实现复杂的游戏（如《Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri》）和用Rust重新实现Linux命令行工具，这些任务要求高智能的AI来完成复杂的工作。
• [rs186] 关注AGI能否优雅地解决Go语言的错误处理问题，提到一个具体的设计草案链接，希望AGI能提供解决方案。
• [kloud] 描述了一个用Clojure构建UI的实验，测试LLM的能力，但遇到Claude Code模型的失败，并计划等待下一轮SOTA模型发布后再尝试。
• [delegate] 质疑Clojure是否已经支持[kloud]所需的功能，并讨论了Clojure现有的特性和工具选择，提出AGI应如何响应这种请求的问题。
• [Lerc] 指出语言创建的定义不明确，未说明是否需要描述、指定或实现某种语言。
• [malux85] 认为AGI的真正测试在于能否解读模糊的要求并实施具体步骤，而不仅仅在于正确完成任务。
• [upghost] 希望有一个能处理Clojure的LLM，不产生低质量代码，并提到简单功能如平衡括号或写合理的ClojureScript也是一个不错的进步。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AGI或LLM能否以及如何有效解决复杂的编程和设计问题，特别是在处理高级任务和模糊要求时。
• 讨论中涉及的具体任务和工具，如Clojure的特性、Linux命令行工具的实现、游戏AI的改进，展示了AGI可能的应用场景和当前技术的局限性。
• 对AGI的能力和任务解释的灵活性也有不同看法，一些人关注实际可操作性，另一些人则关注AGI的智能解读和创新能力。

44621088.article_content:
I propose a new AGI benchmark called CLJ-AGI.
We will know when we have reached AGI when an AI system can do the following:
Input:
I need you to enhance the Clojure language with the changes and features listed below. You are allowed to create a new language. However, if you manage to keep everything backward compatible with existing Clojure, you will be rewarded with a very valuable award by a very special person.
transducer-first design, laziness either eliminated or opt-in
protocols everywhere as much as practically possible (performance)
first-class data structures/types are also CRDT data types, where practical (correctness and performance)
first-class maps, vectors, arrays, sets, counters, and more
Output:
A new (or improved) programming language.

data.title: LLM architecture comparison
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: 本文由Sebastian Raschka博士撰写，比较了从GPT-2到2025年间的多款大型语言模型（LLM）架构，如DeepSeek-V3、Kimi K2和Llama 4。尽管这些模型在细节上有所改进，如位置嵌入从绝对位置变为旋转位置（RoPE），多头注意力（MHA）被分组查询注意力（GQA）取代，激活函数从GELU变为SwiGLU，但核心架构变化不大。文章重点分析了2025年LLM架构的关键变化，尤其是DeepSeek V3引入的多头潜在注意力（MLA）和专家混合（MoE）技术，这些技术提升了模型的计算效率。GQA通过共享键值对减少内存使用，而MLA则通过压缩键值张量进一步节省内存。文章强调，尽管模型性能和训练技术有所不同，但架构上的创新更多是对已有基础的优化而非彻底变革。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）架构的文章及其图表的评价和延伸讨论

不同观点：
• [正面评价] strangescript认为文章中的图表非常好，特别适合处于新手和专家之间的人，能够直观地比较新模型。DeveloperErrata也表示文章教育性强，抽象层次恰到好处，便于学习LLM架构的细节，而不需要费力解析原始论文。ajeet同样感谢作者详细且易于阅读的比较。

• [实用性与更新需求] bravesoul2认为文章对像他这样没有持续关注最新动态的人很有帮助，是一个很好的追赶资料。webappguy则希望看到第二部分，包含闭源前沿模型的传闻信息，如o5、Gemini 2.5 Pro、Grok 4和Claude Opus 4等。

• [技术发展回顾与评价] Chloebaker回顾了自GPT-2以来LLM的快速发展，指出如今比较LLM性能的挑战性，并强调DeepSeek V3在计算效率上的突破和其转型意义。

• [技术局限与未来展望] dmezzetti承认这些架构的创新和改进，但指出生成事实性信息的基本问题仍未解决，提到Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)和Agents等方法的帮助，并展望未来架构是否会取代这些技术。

• [人工智能生成架构] TheDudeMan提到使用Claude生成新架构的实验，但对其质量持不确定态度。

补充讨论：
• krackers提供了与讨论相关的其他资源链接，扩展了讨论的范围。
• 整体讨论显示出对LLM技术进展的关注，以及对未来发展的期待和不确定性。

The Big LLM Architecture Comparison
From DeepSeek-V3 to Kimi K2: A Look At Modern LLM Architecture Design
Sebastian Raschka, PhD
Jul 19, 2025
223
Share this post

The Big LLM Architecture Comparison

Share
It has been seven years since the original GPT architecture was developed. At first glance, looking back at GPT-2 (2019) and forward to DeepSeek-V3 and Llama 4 (2024-2025), one might be surprised at how structurally similar these models still are.
Sure, positional embeddings have evolved from absolute to rotational (RoPE), Multi-Head Attention has largely given way to Grouped-Query Attention, and the more efficient SwiGLU has replaced activation functions like GELU. But beneath these minor refinements, have we truly seen groundbreaking changes, or are we simply polishing the same architectural foundations?
Comparing LLMs to determine the key ingredients that contribute to their good (or not-so-good) performance is notoriously challenging: datasets, training techniques, and hyperparameters vary widely and are often not well documented.
However, I think that there is still a lot of value in examining the structural changes of the architectures themselves to see what LLM developers are up to in 2025. (A subset of them are shown in Figure 1 below.)
Figure 1: A subset of the architectures covered in this article.
So, in this article, rather than writing about benchmark performance or training algorithms, I will focus on the architectural developments that define today's flagship open models.
(As you may remember,
I wrote about multimodal LLMs
not too long ago; in this article, I will focus on the text capabilities of recent models and leave the discussion of multimodal capabilities for another time.)
Tip:
This is a fairly comprehensive article, so I recommend using the navigation bar to access the table of contents (just hover over the left side of the Substack page).
1. DeepSeek V3/R1
As you have probably heard more than once by now,
DeepSeek R1
made a big impact when it was released in January 2025. DeepSeek R1 is a reasoning model built on top of the
DeepSeek V3 architecture
, which was introduced in December 2024.
While my focus here is on architectures released in 2025, I think it’s reasonable to include DeepSeek V3, since it only gained widespread attention and adoption following the launch of DeepSeek R1 in 2025.
If you are interested in the training of DeepSeek R1 specifically, you may also find my article from earlier this year useful:
Understanding Reasoning LLMs
Sebastian Raschka, PhD
·
Feb 5
Read full story
In this section, I’ll focus on two key architectural techniques introduced in DeepSeek V3 that improved its computational efficiency and distinguish it from many other LLMs:
Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)
1.1 Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)
Before discussing Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), let's briefly go over some background to motivate why it's used. For that, let's start with Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), which has become the new standard replacement for a more compute- and parameter-efficient alternative to Multi-Head Attention (MHA) in recent years.
So, here's a brief GQA summary. Unlike MHA, where each head also has its own set of keys and values, to reduce memory usage, GQA groups multiple heads to share the same key and value projections.
For example, as further illustrated in Figure 2 below, if there are 2 key-value groups and 4 attention heads, then heads 1 and 2 might share one set of keys and values, while heads 3 and 4 share another. This reduces the total number of key and value computations, which leads to lower memory usage and improved efficiency (without noticeably affecting the modeling performance, according to ablation studies).
Figure 2: A comparison between MHA and GQA. Here, the group size is 2, where a key and value pair is shared among 2 queries.
So, the core idea behind GQA is to reduce the number of key and value heads by sharing them across multiple query heads. This (1) lowers the model's parameter count and (2) reduces the memory bandwidth usage for key and value tensors during inference since fewer keys and values need to be stored and retrieved from the KV cache.
(If you are curious how GQA looks in code, see my
GPT-2 to Llama 3 conversion guide
for a version without KV cache and my KV-cache variant
here
.)
While GQA is mainly a computational-efficiency workaround for MHA, ablation studies (such as those in the
original GQA paper
and the
Llama 2 paper
) show it performs comparably to standard MHA in terms of LLM modeling performance.
Now, Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) offers a different memory-saving strategy that also pairs particularly well with KV caching. Instead of sharing key and value heads like GQA, MLA compresses the key and value tensors into a lower-dimensional spa

data.title: Async I/O on Linux in databases
data.author: jtregunna
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者在开发简单键值数据库过程中，对I/O性能优化的探索。最初使用内存哈希表和简单的追加日志实现持久化，但性能不佳。之后，作者转向研究Linux的io_uring机制，它通过共享环形缓冲区在应用与内核间实现真正的异步I/O，大幅提升吞吐量。然而，异步I/O导致数据持久性和一致性问题，作者通过引入双写前日志（WAL）设计解决该问题：一个记录操作意图（异步写入），另一个记录操作完成，只有两者齐备时才在恢复时应用操作，确保一致性。最终，作者使用Zig语言实现了该方案，并通过实验验证其性能和可靠性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：io_uring 与同步 API 的性能比较及其在数据库中的应用，特别是关于持久性（durability）和正确性的讨论。

不同观点：
• **quietbritishjim** 认为文章中比较的是有 fsync 调用和无 fsync 调用的性能，而不是同步 API 和 io_uring 的真正性能对比。他认为如果同步代码中去掉 fsync，也能获得类似的性能提升。此外，io_uring 也可以通过某些方法实现 fsync 的功能，因此文章的比较是不对等的。
• **jorangreef** 指出 TigerBeetle 始终使用 fsync 来保证持久性，并且他们的设计目标不是性能而是正确性。TigerBeetle 的双 WAL（写前日志）设计是为了协议感知的恢复，而不是简单的性能优化。
• **sethev** 认为文章中的逻辑有误，指出如果第4步（等待完成记录写入 WAL）正确执行，那么第3步（等待意图记录持久化）就是多余的。他怀疑第4步可能没有正确执行，导致误解。
• **jmpman** 担心如果系统崩溃后，客户端收到成功的请求可能没有对应的完成记录，这违反了 ACID 原则。
• **avinassh** 同意 jmpman 的观点，认为如果完成记录是异步的且可能未完成，那么服务器的持久性保证就会有问题。
• **tlb** 和 **BeeOnRope** 都质疑意图记录的必要性，认为如果只有完成记录是持久化的，那么单独记录意图记录似乎没有意义。
• **leentee** 认为文章中的方案不能保证持久性，并且认为好的同步代码比坏的异步代码更可取，尤其是对于现代 NVMe 存储而言，同步 IO 已经足够快。
• **lstroud** 分享了在 Linux raid 驱动中遇到的死锁问题，并通过移除 lvm 解决了吞吐量问题。
• **ptrwis** 提到目前只有一个人在为 PostgreSQL 实现异步直接 IO。
• **tobias3** 对双 WAL 操作比单个同步 IOPS 更快的说法表示怀疑，认为这可能意味着数据库根本没有持久性。
• **jtregunna** 在更新中澄清了需要等待完成记录写入后再响应客户端，并指出双 WAL 方法在批量处理时有优势，但在接近单次写入时成本更高。
• **ozgrakkurt** 分享了自己实现 crash-resilient LSM 树的经验，并好奇双 WAL 方法与 append/rename 方法的 trade-off。
• **eatonphil** 提到目前似乎没有很多数据库在生产环境中默认使用 io_uring，并希望有人能做这样一个调查。
• **jasonthorsness** 质疑 NVME 存储接口是否应该比 Linux 抽象层更简洁，并提出某些高性能应用可能更适合作为特殊用途的 unikernels。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于文章中比较的合理性和持久性保证，特别是 fsync 在异步和同步代码中的作用。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是双 WAL 设计的必要性和意图记录的作用。
• 一些评论者分享了实际操作中的经验和解决方案，比如 lstroud 的死锁问题和 ozgrakkurt 的 crash-resilient 方法。
• 还有评论者对 io_uring 在生产环境中的使用情况表示关注，并希望有更多调查和数据。

44622454.article_content:
I've been working on a complex multi-model database for a few weeks now, and recently I took time to simplify and test out an idea I had on a simple key-value database. I started with the basics: A hash table in memory, a simple append-only log for persistence and durability, and the classic fsync() call after every write to the log for durability.
It worked, but wasn't as fast as it could be.
In
Kevo
, that's the approach I use, but in Klay (not public yet, but will be open sourced when ready), I'm taking a different approach. What would a database look like if you treated the individual sectors on disk as unreliable, and how could you make it as fast as possible?
That's when I started reading about io_uring on Linux
here (PDF)
and
here
.
io_uring... what?
You can read
Wikipedia
as good as the next person, so let's skip ahead.
The promises seem to good to be true: truly async I/O for all types of operations, not just network sockets. No more thread pools to work around blocking disk I/O, no more complex state machines built around
epoll
... What's the catch?
Well, after doing some reading, the core insight behind io_uring clicked almost immediately. Traditional I/O interfaces force you to think synchronously--you make a system call, the kernel does work, you get a result. But modern storage hardware is inherently parallel. An NVMe SSD can handle thousands of operations simultaneously, and together, each with its own queue. The bottleneck isn't the hardware; it's the software abstraction.
io_uring exposes this parallelism through a pair of ring buffers shared between your application and the kernel. You submit operations to the submission queue (SQ) and collect results from the completion queue (CQ). Instead of one system call per operation, you can submit dozens of operations with a single
io_uring_submit
call.
My first io_uring experiment was simple: Replace my synchronous WAL writes with async ones. Instead of writing each log entry and waiting for completion, I would submit the write operation and continue processing. The results were dramatic--throughput increased by an order of magnitude almost immediately.
But then I started hitting consistency issues...
Durability
The problem with naive async I/O in a database context at least, is that you lose the durability guarantee that makes databases useful. When a client receives a success response, their expectation is the data will survive a system crash. But with async I/O, by the time you send that response, the data might still be sitting in kernel buffers, not yet written to stable storage.
My initial solution was to track pending I/O operations and only return success after the corresponding completion arrived from io_uring. This worked, but it defeated the purpose--I was back to waiting for disk I/O before completing transactions.
Clearly, I need a better approach.
Rethinking my WAL
The traditional
write-ahead log
(WAL) protocol is simple: log the change, force it to disk, then apply it. But what if we could separate the "intent to change" from the "confirmation of the change"? What if we could log our intentions quickly and asynchronously, then confirm completion separately?
That led me to a
TigerBeetle talk
being given by Joran Dirk Greef. Turns out, TigerBeetle uses the same sort of approach. The more I learned about TigerBeetle, the more I had confidence in the approach. (Note: TigerBeetle doesn't externalize commits asynchronously though, see clarification in
this X post
.)
So I set out to experiment with a dual WAL design, in a simple in-memory key-value database, that used the dual WAL design:
Intent WAL
: Records what operations I plan to perform
Completion WAL
: Records successful completion of these operations
So the protocol ends up becoming:
Write intent record (async)
Perform operation in memory
Write completion record (async)
Return success to client
During recovery, I only apply operations that have both intent and completion records. This ensures consistency while allowing much higher throughput.
Building the Dual WAL System
Alright, I'm also using Zig for this, since Klay is being written in Zig, I kept
Poro (GitHub)
using Zig as well to reduce the things I needed to keep in my head at once. In case it's not obvious, and it may not be, Poro is the experimental key-value database with the dual WAL system implemented as a demo.
Implementing this approach requires attention to several details. First, I need to separate io_uring instances--one for each WAL type. This prevents head-of-line blocking where completion writes might wait behind intent writes.
pub const WAL = struct {
intent_ring: io_uring,              // Dedicated ring for intent ops
completion_ring: io_uring,          // Dedicated ring for completions
intent_file_fd: std.posix.fd_t,
completion_file_fd: std.posix.fd_t,
intent_buffer: []u8,                // Circular buffer
completion_buffer: []u8,            // Circular buffer
};
The circular buffers are crucial for performanc

data.author: slacktivism123
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了GitHub上的一个合并请求，涉及为Antiwork项目添加自助邀请链接功能。该功能允许管理员为承包商生成邀请链接，并引导承包商完成认证、入职和文档上传等步骤。关键更新包括：引入邀请链接模型以跟踪邀请信息，支持已认证和未认证用户的邀请流程，改进承包商人页面的UI元素，以及增加全面的测试。此外，还修复了一些错误并进行了若干界面和文字调整。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PR流程中大量提交、自动化工具和机器人的使用是否合理，以及其对开源项目贡献的影响。

不同观点：
• [id00] 认为一个简单的功能不需要如此多的提交和讨论，流程过于繁琐，可能会打击贡献者的积极性。
• [StrLght] 和 [rokkamokka] 对当前的PR流程感到不满，认为自动化工具和机器人评论没有带来相应的价值，反而造成了不必要的干扰。
• [thomascountz] 通过计算器的比喻指出，复杂的工具（如LLM）在某些情况下可能并不适合简单的任务，过度的自动化可能反而让用户感到困惑和负担。
• [slacktivism123] 质疑这种自动化流程是否是协作编程的未来，并指出LLM对小错误进行标记可能带来负面影响。
• [spuz] 建议将反馈功能集成到评论框中，以便在用户写作时提供反馈，而不是事后增加噪音。
• [picafrost] 提出AI的使用可能成为职位描述的一部分，并询问人们在求职时是否关注这方面的内容。
• [r0ckarong] 和 [mykowebhn] 认为这种繁琐的流程会阻碍开源项目的贡献，尤其是不必要的提交历史会污染项目记录。
• [juliangmp] 直接质疑这些机器人的存在价值，表示没有人会需要它们。
• [am17an] 预测未来可能会出现围绕GitHub PR的包装工具来解决这些问题，并暗示当前的自动化流程已经导致了工程师招聘的停止。
• [amiga386] 用激烈的语言表达对机器人的不满，认为机器人没有增加价值，反而可能赶走自愿贡献者。
• [PeterStuer] 讽刺地指出，如果贡献者忘记使用AI工具润色信息会带来的“恐怖”后果。
• [Asraelite] 认为在原则上，机器人检查语法错误和打字错误是可以接受的，但当前的机器人配置过于严苛，坚持不必要的语言规范。

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到机器人评论和自动化流程带来的干扰和噪音问题，尤其是对贡献者积极性和项目效率的影响。

- 关于机器人配置和反馈时机的技术性建议，如[spuz]提出的将反馈集成到评论框中的建议。
- 机器人对项目文化和社区氛围的影响，尤其是对自愿贡献者的驱离效应。

争议焦点：自动化工具和机器人在PR流程中的价值和适用性，以及其对项目贡献和社区氛围的影响。

Self-Serve Invite Link Feature —
Fixes
#348
This feature enables admins to generate an invite link for contractors
Admin Flow
Generate Invite Link
Navigate to the
People
page. Click on the
Invite Link
button.
Generate or Reset Invite Link
Confirm the reset in the dialog.
Contractor Flow
Open Invite Link
The contractor opens the provided invite link in their browser.
Authentication
If not already signed in, clicking
Accept Invite
redirects the contractor to the signup/login page.
Onboarding
After authenticating, the contractor is guided through the initial onboarding steps.
Document Upload
Once onboarding is complete, the user is redirected to the document upload page to continue the process.
Confirmation
After submitting required documents, the contractor sees a confirmation screen indicating successful onboarding.
Approach
1. Invite Link Model
A dedicated model stores invite tokens, along with the inviter, company, and an optional document template ID.
This enables tracking and management of invitations independently from users.
2. Invite Link Usage Scenarios
When a user opens an invite link, two scenarios are handled:
a) Unauthenticated User:
The user is redirected to the sign-up flow.
The
invitation_token
is stored in a cookie for later use.
b) Authenticated User:
The invite accept API is called immediately.
A
company_worker
entry is created for the current user, and the company context is switched.
3. Invite Acceptance and Onboarding
For unauthenticated users:
After sign-up, the system detects the
invitation_token
and uses it to create a
company_worker
entry using the
AcceptInviteLink
service
For authenticated users:
The invite is accepted directly, and the
company_worker
entry is created.
4. Incomplete Contractor Profile
The initial
company_worker
instance created from an invite is incomplete (missing role, rates, etc.).

44622374.article_content:
Blender
MCP
Turning AI into your creative Blender co-pilot.
Realtime 3D Control via Model Context Protocol
Watch
Demo
What is
Blender MCP
?
Blender MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a seamless integration layer that empowers Large Language Models (LLMs) to take control of Blender using simple JSON instructions. It turns AI into a real-time 3D collaborator—through a fast and open TCP-based connection.
Instant AI-to-3D Pipeline
Generate, modify, and animate Blender scenes in real time by connecting any LLM to the MCP server. No plugins, no manual clicks—just pure AI-driven creativity.
Lightweight JSON Protocol
Communicate using clean and structured JSON commands over TCP. Designed for reliability, simplicity, and extensibility—perfect for research and rapid prototyping.
Plug & Play with Any LLM
Easily hook up models like Claude, ChatGPT, or open-source LLMs to your Blender environment. Claude Desktop already supports direct MCP server input—just add your server and start building.
Scene Manipulation
Complete control over 3D scenes, objects, materials, and animations with precise command execution.
Total Scene Control
Create meshes, move objects, apply materials, trigger animations—Blender MCP gives the AI full access to manipulate your 3D world.
Why We Built Blender MCP
Blender MCP was created to establish a standardized, universal interface between Large Language Models and 3D software like Blender—making AI-powered 3D creation accessible, fast, and intuitive.
Whether you're a Blender pro looking to speed up complex workflows or a curious beginner
(like us when we started!)
trying to bring your ideas to life without wrestling with UI or scripting—
Blender MCP bridges that gap
.
We believe the future of 3D content lies in
natural language + real-time control
. This project makes that future usable today.
Project
Details
Code Architecture
TCP Server
Handles incoming connections and JSON command parsing
Command Processor
Translates JSON commands to Blender Python API calls
Scene Controller
Manages 3D scene state and object manipulation

"location": [0, 0, 0],

}
}

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：非侵入式脑机接口（BCI）的可行性及未来发展方向

不同观点：
• 观点1：对非侵入式BCI持怀疑态度。ACCount36认为，EEG（脑电图）作为非侵入式技术存在已有很长时间，但并未成为有效的界面系统，表明其局限性。
  - 论据：EEG技术长期存在但未能实现有用的接口功能。
  - 例子：EEG技术缺乏实际应用中的成功案例。

• 观点2：侵入式BCI是更可行的方向。ACCount36指出，像Neuralink N1这样完全侵入式的BCI，拥有超过1000个记录通道，虽然仅能提供勉强够用的控制界面，但仍是目前最先进的技术（SOTA）。
  - 论据：Neuralink N1的1000多个通道仅能提供基本可靠的控制，显示出现有技术的局限性。
  - 例子：Neuralink N1作为侵入式技术的代表，展示了当前技术的最高水平。

• 观点3：未来BCI的发展依赖于更具侵入性且通道数量更多的接口。ACCount36认为，更好的BCI发展路径在于增加通道数量和侵入性，而不是相反。
  - 论据：增加通道数量和侵入性可以提高BCI的性能。
  - 例子：目前SOTA的技术仍需更多通道和侵入性来实现更可靠的控制。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：非侵入式与侵入式BCI的技术路线选择。ACCount36明确支持侵入式技术，认为非侵入式技术如EEG不具备发展前景，而侵入式技术则是未来的方向。
• 技术现状：当前技术如Neuralink N1虽为最先进，但仍存在性能上的限制，显示出BCI技术整体仍处于发展初期。

总结：评论围绕非侵入式和侵入式BCI的可行性展开讨论，焦点在于技术路线的选择和未来发展方向，一方认为非侵入式技术缺乏实用性，另一方则看好侵入式技术的发展潜力。

data.article_summary: 科学家们首次在传统电子芯片上集成了微小的光子量子系统。这个硅芯片由北western大学、波士顿大学和加州大学伯克利分校的团队开发，尺寸仅为1毫米见方，结合了量子光生成组件和经典电子控制电路。该芯片不仅能产生量子光，还内置智能电子系统以稳定光源，支持量子通信、传感和处理。这种光电集成芯片可以在商业半导体工厂大规模生产，为量子计算、传感和通信应用开辟了新途径。该研究解决了量子系统微型化的挑战，标志着量子技术发展的重要一步。研究成果发表在《Nature Electronics》期刊上。

44586283.article_content:
First electronic-photonic quantum chip manufactured in commercial foundry
First time quantum light sources, control electronics are tightly integrated on a silicon chip
July 14, 2025
| By
Amanda Morris
A packaged circuit board containing the chip placed under microscope in probe station during an experiment. The first-of-its-kind silicon chip combines both the quantum light-generating components (photonics) with classical electronic control circuits — all packed into an area measuring just one millimeter by one millimeter.
Computer Science
Data Science
Innovation
McCormick
For the first time, scientists at Northwestern University, Boston University (BU) and University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley) have built a tiny photonic quantum system into a traditional electronic chip.
The first-of-its-kind silicon chip combines both the quantum light-generating components (photonics) with classical electronic control circuits — all packed into an area measuring just one millimeter by one millimeter. So, not only does the chip generate quantum light, but it also has its own built-in smart electronic system to keep that light perfectly stable.
This photonic-electronic integration enables the single chip to reliably produce a stream of photon pairs — basic units that encode quantum information — required for light-based quantum communication, sensing and processing.
A commercial semiconductor foundry fabricated the chip, demonstrating its ability to be manufactured for large-scale production.
The
study was published i
n the journal
Nature Electronics
.
“Quantum experiments in the lab usually need big, bulky equipment, which requires pristine, clean conditions,” said Northwestern’s Anirudh Ramesh, who led the quantum measurements. “We took many of those electronics and shrunk them down onto one chip. So, now we have a chip with built-in electronic control — stabilizing a quantum process in real time. This is a key step toward scalable quantum photonic systems.”
This is a big deal because it’s not easy to mix electronics and photonics.”
Prem Kumar of the Center for Photonic Communication and Computing
“For the first time, we have achieved monolithic electronic, photonic and quantum integration,” said Northwestern’s
Prem Kumar
, one of the study’s senior authors. “This is a big deal because it’s not easy to mix electronics and photonics. It was a heroic effort that combined expertise from an interdisciplinary, collaborative team of physicists, electrical engineers, computer scientists, materials scientists and manufacturing experts. Our chip could open doors for not only computing but sensing and communication applications.”
An expert in quantum optics, Kumar is a professor of electrical and computer engineering at Northwestern’s
McCormick School of Engineering
, where he directs the
Center for Photonic Communication and Computing
. At the time of the research,
Ramesh was a Ph.D. candidate in Kumar’s laboratory; now he
is a
quantum systems validation engineer
at U.S.-based quantum computing company PsiQuantum.
Ramesh co-led the study with Danielius Kramnik at UC Berkeley and Imbert Wang at BU. Kramnik, who led the circuit design and electronic integration, is a recent Ph.D. graduate from the laboratory of
Vladimir Stojanovíc
, an adjunct professor of electrical engineering and computer sciences at UC Berkeley. Wang, who led the photonic device design, is a recent Ph.D. graduate from the laboratory of
Miloš Popović
, an associate professor of electrical and computer engineering at BU.
Chip produces its own quantum light, stabilizes itself
With their ability to be manufactured using the same high-volume processes that create billions of transistors for everyday electronics, silicon chips are an ideal platform for light-based quantum systems. But stably operating these tiny quantum optical devices requires capabilities that are not currently standard in a commercial foundry. Slight temperature changes, imperceptible manufacturing imperfections and even heat generated by their own components can completely ruin an entire quantum system. To control these tiny variations, researchers have relied on large, external equipment to stabilize quantum optical devices — making it seemingly impossible to miniaturize full systems.
The generation of quantum light in silicon — which the team used in their foundry-manufactured devices — was first demonstrated in a decades-old experiment from Kumar’s lab at Northwestern. In a
2006 study published in the journal Optics Express
